correctness.rationale: For every quiver, direct basis multiplication gives L_x(a)=lambda_source(a)*a and R_x(a)=lambda_target(a)*a; vertex columns contribute one dimension for each nonzero scalar. Modulo those images, zero-scalar vertex columns have disjoint arrow-coordinate supports by target for L_x and source for R_x, adding exactly the numbers of target/source vertices of internally supported arrows. Multiplicity of each disjoint (S,F)-stratum is (q-1)^(n-|S|+|F|) q^(m-|E[S]|), yielding every coefficient. The q>=2 strict inequalities of the three path rank-one coefficients are exact. The Python verifier independently constructs literal multiplication matrices and exhaustively agrees in 56 finite-field configurations; these checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Elia--Gorla establish regular representation rank as a way to compute individual ideal dimensions in group algebras; the claimed coefficient formula is not their result. The assessed claim is the full element-weighted bivariate spectrum (dim xA,dim Ax) for all finite quivers, plus the exact orientation-separation corollary. The closest accessible studies concern conjugacy finiteness of ideals, quiver homological invariants, singular equivalence, or commutator ranks, none of whose inspected statements supplies these generator-weighted two-sided rank coefficients. Priority remains subject to older alternative terminology.

value.rationale: The distribution of dim(xA) and dim(Ax) is an intrinsic, natural element-weighted invariant of any finite-dimensional algebra. In this infinite quiver family the formula gives all joint multiplicities for any finite field, including disconnected graphs, loops and parallel arrows. It directly resolves a structural distinction invisible to commuting tuple equations: the rank-one coefficient separates all three orientations of a 3-vertex path for every finite field. The result is not based on an arbitrary finite slice or a tiny numerical gain; it supplies a general exact invariant and an orientation-reconstruction boundary.
